capture.final_message:
Use the disjoint-cycle decomposition of a finite permutation as the central representation.

- For the first conjunct, show that membership \(c \in g.\mathrm{cycleFactorsFinset}\) implies:
  1. \(c\) is a nontrivial cycle on \(\operatorname{support}(c)\);
  2. \(g\) agrees with \(c\) on that support, since all other cycle factors have disjoint support.

  Hence the orbit of any point under \(g\), while inside \(\operatorname{support}(c)\), is the same as its orbit under \(c\), proving `g.IsCycleOn c.support`.

- For the second conjunct, use the characterization of cycle factors by same-cycle equivalence classes. The permutation `f.cycleOf x` is the cycle factor associated to the class of \(x\). It appears in the decomposition exactly when that cycle is nontrivial, which is equivalent to \(f(x)\ne x\), and hence to \(x\in f.support\).

The `Fintype` and `DecidableEq` assumptions are essential only for constructing the finite supports and the canonical finite set of cycle factors.
